title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Palau: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Palau: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Palau: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Organizing medical, healthcare financing, workplace, estate, and international authentication records in advance in the Republic of Palau helps families coordinate smoothly with Koror and Ngerulmud institutions. Because Palau is a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention and processes estate petitions through existing Trial Division, Court of Common Pleas, and Land Court channels while formal Probate Rules remain in development, advance document clarity prevents costly administrative bottlenecks [1][2][6][7].

steps.title: Healthcare coordination, Healthcare Fund (HCF) coverage, and workplace leave
steps.html:
• Coordinate clinical care, specialist consultations, and potential off-island medical referrals through Ministry of Health and Human Services (MHHS) and Belau National Hospital in Koror (+680 488-2552 / 2553 Administration; +680 488-2558 Emergency Room; 911 for all emergencies, 488-1411 Fire/Ambulance) [10][11].
  • Verify Healthcare Fund (HCF) contribution status and medical savings account eligibility early via Republic of Palau Social Security Administration (ROPSSA) (+680 488-1904 HCF Office) and the HCF online payment portal [8][9][12].
  • Confirm paid sick leave, family-care leave, and medical separation terms directly with the employer's human resources office (including Palau National Government civil service rules or private employment contracts), obtaining written medical statements promptly for extended absence [10].

steps.title: Estate planning, current court procedures, and legal proxy documents
steps.html:
• Prepare or update a clear written Will covering cash, bank accounts, vehicles, and personal property, while verifying customary and Land Court requirements separately for Palauan real estate [6].
  • Note from the Palau Judiciary's Press Release # 26-172 that Palau currently operates without standalone Probate Rules (with draft rules scheduled for public consultation through January 2027), meaning formal petitions rely on standard court forms filed at Office of the Clerk of Courts (Palau Supreme Court) under Trial Division, Court of Common Pleas (claims up to US$ 10,000 excluding land), or Land Court jurisdiction [2][6][7].
  • Prepare a written Power of Attorney or care-authorization document with private counsel or Micronesian Legal Services Corporation (MLSC) (+680 488-2473 / 2474) if trusted family members need authority to manage banking or off-island referral logistics [2].

steps.title: ROPSSA insured quarters, disability, and survivor preconditions
steps.html:
• Review Social Security earnings statements and quarterly contribution records with Republic of Palau Social Security Administration (ROPSSA) (P.O. Box 679, Koror, Palau 96940; Tel +680 488-2457) [8][9].
  • Confirm where the contributor stands relative to ROPSSA thresholds: 38 quarters (9.5 years) or 1 quarter per year between age 21 and eligibility for fully insured status, 8 quarters in the last 13 quarters for currently insured status, and 120 quarters (30 years) for permanently insured status [8].
  • Check disability and retirement application forms and keep marriage certificates and dependent children's birth certificates verified in advance so survivor or incapacity filings require minimal follow-up [2][8].

steps.title: Vital record accuracy, Clerk fees, and tax readiness
steps.html:
• Confirm that names, dates of birth, and family links match across birth certificates, marriage records, passports, Social Security cards, and land deeds [2][3][8]. Certified vital record copies from Office of the Clerk of Courts (Palau Supreme Court) in Koror (+680 488-2607 / 3331 / 4979, Ngerulmud +680 767-2607, Monday to Friday 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM) cost US$ 2.00 locally or US$ 15.00 for off-island requests [2][4][5].
  • Verify personal wage, business gross revenue, and Palau Goods and Services Tax (PGST) filings so accounts are orderly; Palau does not impose a separate inheritance or estate tax [9].
  • Keep original signed legal documents, HCF statements, and certified civil records together in an accessible, dry location known to trusted family members [2][3].

steps.title: Hague Apostille readiness and household inventory
steps.html:
• Because Palau is a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (in force since 23 June 2020), any certified Palau vital certificate or court order needed by foreign banks, insurers, or U.S./foreign registries can receive an Apostille from either designated Competent Authority: the Minister of State (Koror, +680 767-2408) or the Clerk of Courts, Palau Supreme Court [1].
  • Build a clear written household inventory covering Social Security and HCF numbers, Koror/off-island bank accounts, insurance policies, employer contacts, Land Court or Bureau of Lands deeds, and safe-deposit details [2][6][8].
  • Check receiving-country translation or notarization requirements early if international heirs or institutions will handle cross-border funds [1][2].

contacts.name: Ministry of Health and Human Services (MHHS)
contacts.note: Operates Belau National Hospital in Koror (+680 488-2552/2553 Admin; +680 488-2558 Emergency Room; 911 emergency line).

contacts.name: Republic of Palau Social Security Administration (ROPSSA)
contacts.note: Administers Social Security quarters, disability/retirement benefits, and Healthcare Fund (+680 488-1904).

contacts.name: Office of the Clerk of Courts (Palau Supreme Court)
contacts.note: Maintains vital statistics ($2.00 local / $15.00 off-island certified copies), accepts estate petitions, and issues 1961 Hague Apostilles.

contacts.name: Micronesian Legal Services Corporation (MLSC)
contacts.note: Legal aid service assisting eligible residents with civil planning, Powers of Attorney, and court matters (+680 488-2473 / 488-2474).
